title: Philosophy
coreMove: Hold a large question long enough to separate inherited doctrine from values you can test and live by.
sourcePressure: The source offers three answers to meaning, then turns to values, honesty, long-term relationships, peer relationships, anger, rational Buddhism, evolution, skepticism toward unverifiable claims, wisdom, and the present. It asks the reader to discover and verify rather than accept doctrine.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The wrong version turns this into purpose-finding, abstract spirituality, nihilism, or quote-driven philosophy. This chapter must keep philosophy practical: what can you verify, what will you not compromise, and what does the present ask you to live now.

hook: staring at stars and asking the meaning of life
counterintuition: life has no meaning so you create your own
philosophy must be lived, not studied
the present is all we have
tryThisNow: write your values in a notebook
sit quietly with a big question
ask what you would do if today were your last day

exampleSpecs.domain: family-owned quarry deciding whether to sell stone to a developer known for short-term breaches
exampleSpecs.audience: an owner whose inherited business code is being tested by a lucrative order
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether stated long-term values survive a contract that would reward short-term dealing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he places the developer's late-payment record beside the signed family credit policy and declines the order before the discount offer can become the real rule
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A limestone sample sits on top of a stained family credit policy.

exampleSpecs.domain: urban planner testing whether her anti-car identity is blocking a safer street design
exampleSpecs.audience: a policy professional whose label is starting to decide before the facts do
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a neighborhood gets a performative plan or one that actually lowers injuries
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: before presenting, she removes the slogan slide, overlays crash data with delivery access, and keeps the protected turn lane because the facts survive her label
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A transparent crash map is clipped over a street-section drawing.

exampleSpecs.domain: monastery archivist rejecting a miracle claim after examining the preservation conditions
exampleSpecs.audience: a respectful seeker who wants spiritual practice without surrendering verification
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether reverence becomes credulity or remains honest inquiry
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she notes the sealed box, low humidity, and replaced binding, then keeps the meditation practice while crossing out the miracle explanation in the archive note
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A cracked prayer book lies in a sealed cedar archive box.

exampleSpecs.domain: cooperative bakery choosing peer governance after a founder keeps drifting into boss mode
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder who claims to value peers but enjoys being obeyed
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the stated value of peer relationships changes pay, voice, and decision rights
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: when a baker says the vote is fake if one person can overrule it, the founder rewrites the decision rule on the order board and steps out of the tiebreaker role
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A flour-dusted order board lists tomorrow's bake beside a crossed-out veto rule.

exampleSpecs.domain: retired boxer deciding whether anger still belongs in his coaching after a teenager flinches
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach whose old identity treats anger as useful fuel
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether an inherited emotional tool keeps harming the people he claims to train
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he sees the teenager flinch at the mitt slap, lowers the pad, and writes a new rule that correction cannot require fear
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A worn focus mitt hangs from one hand beside an empty ring corner.

exampleSpecs.domain: astrophotographer leaving a failed eclipse shot undeleted to practice the present over the trophy
exampleSpecs.audience: a maker who turns rare beauty into a possession test
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the event is lost twice: once to clouds and again to resentment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she stops hunting for a salvageable frame, leaves the blurred corona on the camera screen, and looks up while the last light is still changing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A blurred eclipse corona glows on the back of a camera screen.

skillTargets: separate a lived value from a stated preference in a concrete decision
test a spiritual or philosophical claim without mocking or blindly accepting it
recognize when identity is making a belief package feel mandatory
apply long-term and peer values under pressure from money or hierarchy
evaluate whether a response honors the present or tries to possess what is passing

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one value you claim to live by. Find the next choice today where it costs you something small, then remove the option that would let you keep the slogan without paying the cost.

sourceAnchors.name: Osho
sourceAnchors.detail: the source uses Osho’s image of writing on water or building houses of sand while discussing the absence of intrinsic meaning
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Osho’s image keeps the nihilism from sounding abstract: write on water, build in sand, then decide how to live anyway.

sourceAnchors.name: Richard Feynman
sourceAnchors.detail: the source invokes Feynman’s turtles-all-the-way-down image to show why every proposed ultimate meaning invites another why
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Feynman’s infinite stack of whys keeps the question honest instead of letting the first answer harden into doctrine.

sourceAnchors.name: Charlie Munger
sourceAnchors.detail: the source quotes Munger on becoming worthy of a worthy mate while discussing values and relationships
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Munger’s line turns values from a list into a demand: become the kind of person the relationship would require.

sourceAnchors.name: The Iliad
sourceAnchors.detail: the source includes Homer’s Iliad line about beauty under doom in the section on the present
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The Iliad lands because it makes impermanence sharpen the moment instead of draining it.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: prevents the timestamp+named-protagonist template from dominating the chapter

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm — a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following 'concrete anchor -> abstract rule -> elaboration'
